RFC7313-4-1.note: Single-polarity positive, marker accepted: no input selects a re-advertisement without the BoRR and Ze's receipt of BoRR/EoRR is log-only (4-4/4-5 gaps), so neither a refusal path nor a handling-of-absence negative exists; no negative tag exists to hold. The peer-requested clause is now proven: TestRFC7313BoRRRoutesEoRRInOneSequence logs markers and routes in one order on both rails (handleRefresh, handleRefreshStructured) and asserts [BoRR, route, route, EoRR]; observed red with handleRefresh broken. The BoRR is written raw at once and the routes only after it, so no engine queue can put a route ahead of it. Still unproven: the 'initiated locally' clause. Ze has no locally initiated refresh (the only BoRR producers are the two peer-request handlers; soft clear sends an inbound ROUTE-REFRESH). The main thread has ruled that clause is R3-split into its own row excluded as feature-out-of-scope; once split, this row's remaining clause is enforced on the unit above.

RFC7313-4-2.note: Single-polarity positive, marker accepted (same reasoning as 4-1). Proven at the RIB: TestRFC7313BoRRRoutesEoRRInOneSequence asserts on both rails that the EoRR is the last entry, after both IPv4 unicast routes of the family's Adj-RIB-Out, with the IPv6 route absent; observed red with sendRoutes broken. Missing: the order on the wire. The EoRR leaves through reactorAPIAdapter.sendRouteRefresh -> Peer.SendRawMessage immediately, while each re-advertised route goes through the announce path, which diverts it into the peer's opQueue while peer.shouldQueue() holds (initial-sync window). A refresh answered in that window would put the EoRR ahead of the routes; suspected, not reproduced (plan/journal/marker-overtakes-the-queue-it-brackets.md). Needs a whole-Peer test reading the wire order for a refresh during initial sync.

RFC7313-4-3.note: (a) forbidden: handling a ROUTE-REFRESH without reading its subtype (every subtype treated alike); (b) no tagged assertion goes red on it. TestHandleRouteRefreshBoRR, TestHandleRouteRefreshEoRR, TestHandleRouteRefreshUnknown and TestHandleRouteRefresh_UnknownSubtype all assert only NoError and Established, the same outcome for every subtype, so a subtype-blind handler passes all of them. The differentiated action (only subtype 0 starts a refresh) lives in rib_structured.go and rs parseStructuredRefresh and is asserted only by an untagged rib test for subtype 1.

RFC7313-5-1.note: (a) forbidden: not sending Error 7/subcode 1 for a BoRR or EoRR whose body is not 4 octets; (b) TestRouteRefreshBadLengthByMessageSubtype asserts the exact NOTIFICATION for subtypes 1 and 2, too short and too long, and TestRouteRefreshInvalidLengthNotDelivered asserts octets 7/1. Negatives: subtype 0 draws Bad Message Length, a peer without capability 70 draws Bad Message Length, a 4-octet body draws nothing, and an unknown subtype of any length draws no NOTIFICATION and is not delivered (TestRouteRefreshUnknownSubtypeIsIgnoredWhateverItsLength, whose well-formed cases now expect 0 deliveries after the RFC7313-5-3 fix).

RFC7313-5-3.note: Forbidden: acting on a ROUTE-REFRESH whose subtype is not 0, 1 or 2. Defect fixed at the producer: screenRouteRefresh now calls routeRefreshSubtypeUnknown (peer sent capability 70), so the read path drops the message before onMessageReceived. TestRouteRefreshUnknownSubtypeNeverDelivered asserts 0 onMessageReceived and 0 onRefreshRecv, no NOTIFICATION and Established for 4-octet subtypes 3/5/42/255; negative: subtypes 0/1/2 through the same exchange are delivered once each. TestRouteRefreshUnknownSubtypeIsIgnoredWhateverItsLength extends this to wrong-length unknown subtypes (0 deliveries, no NOTIFICATION). The session_test.go units prove only no teardown.
